quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When stopping your car on the roadside in an emergency, you do not need to set the parking brake.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Always set your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop. Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow X on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to change to a red X.
The signal is about to change to a green arrow.
You may drive normally in this lane.
You may drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The signal is about to change to a red X.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed throughout the day. A solid yellow X means you should leave the lane immediately. A red X will appear next.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge their distance and speed. Always stay alert around motorcycles.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand point downward. What does this signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A left arm and hand pointing downward means the driver is stopping. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: What do round signs warn about?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Railroad crossings ahead.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you about railroad crossings. Drive with extra care when you see this sign.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and check for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a green light unless a sign says not to. You must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.
No passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is coming. The road splits into two separate one-way roads. Stay to the right.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn left after checking for other traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and other traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and children are playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so children hear you.
Walk behind your car to check it is clear.
Tell the children to stay away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk behind your car to check it is clear.
questions.explanation: Always look through your back window and mirrors before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially with children nearby. Get out and check behind your car before backing.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel the opposite way.
Turn the wheel toward traffic.
Turn the wheel in the direction of the skid.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, stay calm. Steer the wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines are doubled in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that the road ahead has low clearance.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making a turn.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed. Solid lines cannot be crossed. You may only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a slope with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. This keeps your vehicle from rolling into traffic. If there is no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system cause?

options.text: Excessive oil use.
Your vehicle needs a tune-up sooner.
Drowsiness while driving.
Grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drowsiness while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases and cools hot gases from the engine. Leaking exhaust fumes are dangerous and can cause drowsiness while driving.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is present danger.
Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
Warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing rules, and other driving rules.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a fire hydrant.

options.text: 40 feet
20 feet
10 feet
5 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant. Park where others can see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: What do diamond symbols on pavement markings and signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
Carpool lanes.
Construction areas.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carpool lanes.
questions.explanation: Diamond symbols mark carpool lanes. These lanes require at least two people in the vehicle. They are usually on the far left of a freeway and separated by white or yellow lines.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?

options.text: Your own reaction time.
The time of day.
The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
The condition and type of your vehicle's tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to travel under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the legal maximum or minimum speed for ideal conditions. You can drive slower, but not faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or bad weather.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You may never stop your vehicle there.
You may park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You may stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You may stop to load or unload merchandise.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only make a short stop to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a circular red light.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic must move in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a circular red light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a circular red light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What should you do first when visibility is reduced?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see well, reduce your speed first. This is your most important response to poor visibility and dangerous road conditions.

questions.question: When may you drive faster than the posted speed limit?

options.text: Never.
When legally passing another vehicle on a highway with a speed limit of 55 mph or higher.
When there is no police officer present.
When you are in a hurry.

questions.correctAnswerText: When legally passing another vehicle on a highway with a speed limit of 55 mph or higher.
questions.explanation: You cannot legally drive faster than the posted limit. The only exception is when passing another vehicle on a highway with a speed limit of 55 mph or higher. Then you can go 10 mph faster.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers to keep right to avoid a potential hazard ahead.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Take the right-of-way since you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You can enter the intersection when the light is green to prepare for your left turn. Wait in the center until approaching traffic clears before you turn.

questions.question: You may not park within ____ of a railroad crossing.

options.text: 15 feet
25 feet
40 feet
50 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. Park where other drivers can see your vehicle clearly from both directions.

questions.question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless they are with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run in front of your vehicle without looking.

questions.question: You should allow more space between your vehicle and the car ahead when stopping:

options.text: On an incline.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On an incline.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle on an uphill slope. If the vehicle ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, you will have room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: You must pull over and let an emergency vehicle pass:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is following you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether it is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road.
Demand the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, allow vehicles going the opposite direction at least half the main road. Both vehicles need space to pass safely.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: A series of curves is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has three or more curves coming up.

questions.question: At an intersection where you must stop but no stop line or crosswalk is marked, you should:

options.text: Not stop.
Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet on each side, even if you enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where you have a clear view of approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you have a clear view of approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting road where you can see approaching traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: A traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection. You should:

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop immediately.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that give directions and distances to drivers.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to specific places. They help you when driving in unfamiliar areas.
